pll1d17c1-d1e3477.summary: Turns to assigning the Spirit's invisible mission into the hearts of the faithful. The Spirit, God and third person, proceeds temporally from Father, Son, and himself, that is, is sent and given to the faithful; what this mission is and how it happens must be considered.
claims: The Spirit is sent and given invisibly to the faithful.

pll1d17c1-d1e3480.summary: States a necessary premise: the Spirit, the love of Father and Son by which they love each other and us, is also the love or charity by which we love God and neighbor. When charity makes us love God and neighbor, the Spirit is said to be sent or given, and loving the love by which we love our neighbor is loving God, since that love is God, the Holy Spirit.
claims: The Holy Spirit is the charity by which we love God and neighbor.
The Spirit is given when charity makes us love God and neighbor.
To love the love by which we love our neighbor is to love God.

pll1d17c1-d1e3493.summary: Proposes to confirm the claim by authorities, lest anything seem to be added of his own in so great a matter.

pll1d17c1-d1e3497.summary: Cites De Trinitate VIII: whoever loves his neighbor must above all love love itself, and since God is love, he must above all love God.
claims: Loving the neighbor implies loving love itself.
Since God is love, loving the neighbor implies loving God.

pll1d17c1-d1e3525.summary: Further De Trinitate VIII: why run to heaven and earth seeking God, who is with us? Let one love the brother and love that love; he knows the love by which he loves better than the brother, so God can be better known than the brother, as more present, inward, and certain. Love unites angels and God's servants, and whoever is full of love is full of God.
claims: God, who is love, is present to us.
We know the love by which we love better than the brother we love.
God can be better known to us than our brother.
Whoever is full of love is full of God.

pll1d17c1-d1e3558.summary: Notes that Augustine thereby shows that the love by which we love God or neighbor is God.
claims: The love by which we love God and neighbor is God.

pll1d17c1-d1e3564.summary: Adds Augustine's reading of 1 John: John places the perfection of justice in fraternal love and seems silent about love of God only because he wants God understood in fraternal love. 'Love is from God... God is love' (1 John 4:7–8) shows that fraternal love is not only from God but is God. So in loving the brother from love, we love him from God and necessarily love above all the love itself.
claims: John places perfect justice in love of the brother.
God is understood in fraternal love.
Fraternal love is both from God and God.

pll1d17c1-d1e3618.summary: Further Augustine: whoever does not love his brother is not in love, and whoever is not in love is not in God, for God is love.
claims: One who does not love the brother is not in God.

pll1d17c1-d1e3643.summary: Concludes that Augustine most openly said fraternal love is God.
claims: Fraternal love is God.

pl-l1d17c1.summary: Turns to the Spirit's invisible mission into the hearts of the faithful and lays down a premise necessary for understanding it: the Spirit, already shown to be the love of Father and Son, is also the charity by which we love God and neighbor. When this charity makes us love God and neighbor, the Spirit is said to be sent or given, and whoever loves the very love by which he loves his neighbor loves God, since that love is God. Lombard backs this with De Trinitate VIII: God, who is love, is nearer and better known to us than the brother we love, and from 1 John Augustine concludes that fraternal love is not only from God but is God.
claims: The Spirit is sent invisibly into the hearts of the faithful.
The Holy Spirit is the charity by which we love God and neighbor.
When this charity causes us to love God and neighbor, the Spirit is said to be sent or given.
Whoever loves the love by which he loves his neighbor loves God, since that love is God.
The love by which we love is better known to us than the brother we love.
Fraternal love is God.
